family_summary.text: The observed orientation (longitudinal) points to the lengthwise family of band mechanisms (bands along the rolling direction at fixed width positions). The leading hypothesis (nozzle_thermal_stripe) belongs to the lengthwise family.

below_bite_model_floor.text: No roll-bite result exists for P4 0.035->0.018 mm (18 um): the exit gauge is below the 20 um floor of both roll-bite models (chatter.BitePass.validate). For such a pass the chatter, lever, process-friction fixed point (and pass heating) and gauge-control sections are not assessable, and its strip-shape chain runs only with supplied width_model.shape_inputs (case pass). Collector foil of 16-18 um may in practice be rolled as a DOUBLED (two-sheet) pass, which the tool does not model at all. Ask the plant: single-sheet or doubled?

bite.fallback_reason: Hitchcock contact radius ratio 1.775 exceeds max_radius_ratio 1.5: circular flattening is outside its envelope; a foil (non-circular) contact model or supplied sensitivities are needed
bite.reliability: EXPERIMENTAL elastic-foundation (mattress) foil model with a foundation modulus from a memory formula and no elastic strip zones (forward slip flagged implausible); not validated; it models the contact on the strip only, not the load the rolls carry outside the strip in closed gap.
bite.reported_load_basis: 0.9-2.3 kN/mm of width for battery-foil passes [V S3, S4; conversion D]

foil_regime.case_position_text: 35 um is below every reported closed-gap onset (50-200 um): the work rolls very likely touch outside the strip.
foil_regime.closed_gap_note: Reported onsets of closed-gap rolling disagree (50-200 um exit gauge); the tool has no roll-kissing model.

closed_gap_onset_sources.text: rolls touch outside the strip at 0.1-0.2 mm

closed_gap_onset_sources.source: S16 Publitec, The engineering design of rolling mill
closed_gap_onset_sources.text: below 100 um, about 80 um; force ineffective for gauge below 50 um

closed_gap_onset_sources.source: S17 Jiangsu Huafeng foil flatness note

implications: In closed gap the load is no longer a gauge actuator: more screw-down only bends the rolls and changes flatness; the gauge is set by tension, speed and lubrication [V S8, S16, S17].

The lever table (critical chatter speed against friction, reduction, tensions, span, damping) and the gauge-control section assume an OPEN roll gap; read them as open-gap reasoning, not as foil-mill predictions.

The local transfer of a roll stripe to the strip is by roll / strip compliance, which the shape chain models, but without the load shunted outside the strip where the rolls touch; the transfer may be misestimated.

Online (shapemeter) and offline flatness diverge at foil gauge: front tension masks the true shape [V S17, S8]; the in-mill and after-release states of the shape chain are the tool's proxy for that difference.
Foil band defects with no physical model in the tool (tension lines, hot spots from roll wipers, creasing from ironing rolls) are screened by rules only.
limitations: No roll-kissing (closed-gap) model; the bite models see only the strip contact.
Foil facts are cited from a research pass (tags V / D / M), not plant-validated.

product_question.text: Ask the plant which product this is: 25-60 um can be pouch-laminate barrier foil (8021 / 8079, annealed O temper, 35-50 um), thick collector foil (1235 / 1060 / 1070 / 1100-H18, 21-35 um), or an intermediate pass of thinner collector foil; a final pass of 16-18 um (plant statement) points to cathode current-collector foil in H18 with 25-60 um as intermediate passes. Ask also whether the last pass is single-sheet or doubled (doubling starts at about 18-32 um entry, or not at all for two-side-bright foil [V S3]). O against H18 changes buckling and winding behaviour; this case uses temper H18.

inputs.name: battery_foil_demo
notes: Closed-loop demo: planted causes are a partly blocked nozzle (continuous band hidden under mill tension, visible after tension release, nozzle_thermal_stripe) and a cooling-zone valve closure (cooling_zone_switching_transient).
At 35 um the mill is in or near closed-gap rolling, which the tool does not model: see the foil-regime block. The lever table and the gauge-control section assume an open gap.

Phase-1 coolant section kept consistent with width_model.spray_header; its geometric screen can only represent a FULLY blocked nozzle, so nozzle 11 is listed as blocked there although width_model gives it flow level 0.45.

worse_at_lower_tension is left null although the model in-mill onset of the stripe falls with tension (6.5 um at 40 MPa, 1.5 um at 8 MPa): a band hidden under tension is also "worse at lower tension", so this observation does not separate foil tension lines from a latent thermal stripe.

Final pass 0.035 -> 0.018 mm (collector foil, plant final gauge 16-18 um): below the 20 um roll-bite floor; flag EXIT_GAUGE_BELOW_BITE_MODEL_FLOOR; its rows are reported as not assessable. Ask the plant whether this pass is single-sheet or doubled.
inputs.provenance: SYNTHETIC demonstration, not plant data, for EV battery cathode current-collector foil (1235-H18-like) with a final gauge of 16-18 um and intermediate gauges of 25-60 um. Foil mill: single-stand four-high, work roll 0.27 m diameter (230-330 mm reported, 260-280 typical [V S8]), backup roll 0.75 m (2.8 x the work roll; 2.4-2.8 x reported [V S8]), barrel 1.5 m, strip 1.2 m centred. Half-stack masses and stiffnesses are planner ESTIMATES scaled from the sheet demo mill [D]: work roll 1100 kg (steel barrel pi*0.135^2*1.5*7850 = 674 kg plus necks and chocks), backup roll 9000 kg (barrel 5200 kg plus necks and chocks), work/backup contact 2.0e10 N/m (shorter, smaller-diameter contact than the sheet mill 4e10), housing 6.0e9 N/m (lighter foil stand; sheet mill 1.4e10); 3 m free spans. Schedule 0.26 -> 0.135 -> 0.068 -> 0.035 -> 0.018 mm (48 %, 50 %, 49 %, 49 % per pass): the published battery-foil passes of 48-54 % [V S3, S4] go above the tool's 50 % reduction limit, so the schedule keeps each pass at or below 50 %. The pass 0.068 -> 0.035 mm is the case pass; the final pass 0.035 -> 0.018 mm (180 MPa, 38 / 42 MPa, 15 m/s) is listed so that the report shows what the tool cannot say about it: its exit gauge is below the 20 um floor of both roll-bite models, so its schedule and gauge-trend rows are not assessable (it may also be a doubled pass in practice, not modelled). 1235-H18-like supplied mean flow stress 150 / 165 / 175 MPa (stock UTS 150-200 MPa in H18 [V S4]; no hardening law), friction 0.03 on every pass, tensions 30-35 / 35-40 MPa (entry 29-49, exit 34-44 MPa reported [V S3]), exit speeds 8 / 11 / 13 m/s (600-1000 m/min reported [V S3, S4]), bite_model auto (Hitchcock solves P1 and P2; it rejects the case pass and the experimental mattress model solves it, 1.1 kN/mm of width, inside the 0.9-2.3 kN/mm reported [V S3, S4]). Oil 1.6 mPa s (1.8-2.1 mm2/s at about 0.8 kg/l [V S3, S4]), work-roll Rq 0.15 um (Ra 0.11-0.125 um [V S3, S4] x 1.25 [D]), strip Rq 0.2 um. Neat-oil spray header: 28 nozzles at 52 mm pitch, mean spray coefficient 2 kW/m2K (CHOSEN lower than the 3 kW/m2K emulsion value of the sheet demo [D]; thermal crown 5.0 um). PLANTED CAUSES: nozzle 11 (0.62 m) PARTLY blocked at flow level 0.45, and a 20 s closure of the zone valve of nozzles 18-19. Observations were GENERATED FROM THE MODEL ITSELF (cells 256, default thermal numerics): band positions = model steady stripe peak and event stripe peak rounded to 1 mm (0.623, 0.988 m); the model bands are LATENT under the 40 MPa mill tension and MANIFEST after tension release, so visible_only_after_tension_release is true and the appearance loose_or_buckle; intermittent duration = model visible time of the event band after tension release rounded to 10 s (150 s: at foil gauge the after-release threshold is about 0.2 um of stripe, so even a 20 s valve closure leaves a band for minutes); continuity both; positions repeat across coils and do not move after a work-roll change; the bands change with coolant zone switching; they do not change after roll wiper cleaning and do not track speed changes (a thermal stripe follows heat input slowly). worse_at_thinner_gauge is left NULL: on this mill the model gauge trend does NOT reproduce it (the onset heights rise toward the thin pass). The case therefore tests the screening logic at foil gauge, not the physics.

limitations: Screening result on unvalidated, uncalibrated models; no plant validation is claimed.
The score is an ordinal evidence tally (supports 3/2/1 minus contradictions 6/2/1 for strong/moderate/weak), not a probability and not a certified cause.
The chatter model is linear: it cannot predict limit-cycle amplitude, mark severity or strip break, and a forced response at an unstable operating point is formal only.
Strip spans are lumped springs (inaccurate near the span wave resonance c/(2L)).
Circular (Hitchcock) roll flattening is not valid toward foil gauges; thinner passes need supplied bite sensitivities (model_options.bite_response_override).
The bite-damping closure (fraction beta of transit time) is a declared heuristic; results without it (beta = 0) are reported alongside.
Friction is an input unless tribology.use_computed_friction is set; the friction-speed closure of bite_tribology is an unfitted placeholder whose slope, not level, is used.
Fifth-octave regeneration (backup-roll marking) is screened kinematically, not simulated in time; the antisymmetric mode frequency is an undamped lumped estimate.
Spray coverage is a geometric footprint count; the phase-1 thermal growth is a free-expansion upper bound with no axial conduction (the v2 width_model solves the roll temperature field instead).
The lengthwise physics (roll thermal stripes, shape chain, coil ridges, troughs) rests on planner-derived and memory formulas flagged in each result; no plant validation.

friction.note: PLACEHOLDER friction closure (not fitted): with ground-roll roughness it stays near the boundary regime; read the absolute friction as a placeholder and the slope with speed (dmu/du) as the useful output. With use_computed_friction the friction is a fixed point friction -> bite -> R' -> friction (at most 5 passes, tolerance 0.0001); otherwise it is evaluated once at the contact radius of the supplied-friction bite.

provenance: SYNTHETIC demonstration, not plant data, for EV battery cathode current-collector foil (1235-H18-like) with a final gauge of 16-18 um and intermediate gauges of 25-60 um. Foil mill: single-stand four-high, work roll 0.27 m diameter (230-330 mm reported, 260-280 typical [V S8]), backup roll 0.75 m (2.8 x the work roll; 2.4-2.8 x reported [V S8]), barrel 1.5 m, strip 1.2 m centred. Half-stack masses and stiffnesses are planner ESTIMATES scaled from the sheet demo mill [D]: work roll 1100 kg (steel barrel pi*0.135^2*1.5*7850 = 674 kg plus necks and chocks), backup roll 9000 kg (barrel 5200 kg plus necks and chocks), work/backup contact 2.0e10 N/m (shorter, smaller-diameter contact than the sheet mill 4e10), housing 6.0e9 N/m (lighter foil stand; sheet mill 1.4e10); 3 m free spans. Schedule 0.26 -> 0.135 -> 0.068 -> 0.035 -> 0.018 mm (48 %, 50 %, 49 %, 49 % per pass): the published battery-foil passes of 48-54 % [V S3, S4] go above the tool's 50 % reduction limit, so the schedule keeps each pass at or below 50 %. The pass 0.068 -> 0.035 mm is the case pass; the final pass 0.035 -> 0.018 mm (180 MPa, 38 / 42 MPa, 15 m/s) is listed so that the report shows what the tool cannot say about it: its exit gauge is below the 20 um floor of both roll-bite models, so its schedule and gauge-trend rows are not assessable (it may also be a doubled pass in practice, not modelled). 1235-H18-like supplied mean flow stress 150 / 165 / 175 MPa (stock UTS 150-200 MPa in H18 [V S4]; no hardening law), friction 0.03 on every pass, tensions 30-35 / 35-40 MPa (entry 29-49, exit 34-44 MPa reported [V S3]), exit speeds 8 / 11 / 13 m/s (600-1000 m/min reported [V S3, S4]), bite_model auto (Hitchcock solves P1 and P2; it rejects the case pass and the experimental mattress model solves it, 1.1 kN/mm of width, inside the 0.9-2.3 kN/mm reported [V S3, S4]). Oil 1.6 mPa s (1.8-2.1 mm2/s at about 0.8 kg/l [V S3, S4]), work-roll Rq 0.15 um (Ra 0.11-0.125 um [V S3, S4] x 1.25 [D]), strip Rq 0.2 um. Neat-oil spray header: 28 nozzles at 52 mm pitch, mean spray coefficient 2 kW/m2K (CHOSEN lower than the 3 kW/m2K emulsion value of the sheet demo [D]; thermal crown 5.0 um). PLANTED CAUSES: nozzle 11 (0.62 m) PARTLY blocked at flow level 0.45, and a 20 s closure of the zone valve of nozzles 18-19. Observations were GENERATED FROM THE MODEL ITSELF (cells 256, default thermal numerics): band positions = model steady stripe peak and event stripe peak rounded to 1 mm (0.623, 0.988 m); the model bands are LATENT under the 40 MPa mill tension and MANIFEST after tension release, so visible_only_after_tension_release is true and the appearance loose_or_buckle; intermittent duration = model visible time of the event band after tension release rounded to 10 s (150 s: at foil gauge the after-release threshold is about 0.2 um of stripe, so even a 20 s valve closure leaves a band for minutes); continuity both; positions repeat across coils and do not move after a work-roll change; the bands change with coolant zone switching; they do not change after roll wiper cleaning and do not track speed changes (a thermal stripe follows heat input slowly). worse_at_thinner_gauge is left NULL: on this mill the model gauge trend does NOT reproduce it (the onset heights rise toward the thin pass). The case therefore tests the screening logic at foil gauge, not the physics.
recommended_next_measurements: Spray footprint check (pattern paper or water test) and header inspection; compare the band positions on three consecutive coils with the nozzle positions on the barrel coordinate; shapemeter zone map.
Log the coolant valve states against the shapemeter zones and the band appearance times; compare the band duration with the valve-off intervals.
Vary the span tension and watch the bands; check roll alignment and crown of the deflector / idler rolls; measure the trough spacing.
Record whether the marks appear on both strip faces or only one.
Entry profile scan of the incoming coil and an outside-profile scan of the wound coil (ridges; worse toward the outer wraps?).
Step the exit tension and note whether (and at which tension) the bands fade.
Change the ironing-roll pressure (per side) and, separately, the exit air blow-off, one at a time.
Record whether the bands started when a wider coil followed a narrower one.
Compare the online shapemeter flatness with the offline sag of a sample laid flat (front tension masks the true shape at foil gauge).

limitations: Ignores entry/exit bending at deflector rolls and coilers, which is screened separately by yield_point_bending_window.
reasons: Pass thickness strain 0.6642 (reduction 0.485 > 0.02) exceeds the Luders strain 0.0000: the bite strains the whole strip through the plateau, and the cold work suppresses later yield-point marks. Only skin passes, levelling or bending can leave Luders bands.

limitations: Geometric footprint count only: no flow-rate distribution across the fan, no heat-transfer coefficient, no drift or deflection.

reasons: 27 of 28 nozzles active; effective footprint 0.1667 m vs pitch 0.0520 m (overlap fraction 0.688).

limitations: Free expansion with no axial heat conduction overestimates the growth of a narrow hot stripe, possibly by a large factor.

reasons: Free-expansion radius growth 1.580e-05 m closes the local gap by 9.026e-01 of the exit gauge.

source_disagreements: Effect of friction on chatter is disputed: Yarita (high friction worse), Chefneux (low friction worse), Kimura et al. 2003 (an optimum band). This model gives whatever its slab-derived sensitivities give; see the lever table.
Effect of tension is disputed: Heidari (little effect) vs Zeng, Zang & Gao 2016 (higher tension lowers the critical speed).
The lumped-spring strip span is inaccurate near the span axial wave resonance c/(2L) (about 640 Hz for a 4 m aluminium span); Niroomand et al. 2015 compare lumped and wave span models.

gauge_trend.text: Same 1.43 um roll stripe on every pass, 0.135 mm -> 0.035 mm: linear-feedback I-units 62.9 -> 12.5 (x0.20; rigid bound x3.86). In the mill this stripe buckles on 1 of 3 passes (utilisation 3.2e+03 -> 0); after tension release on 3 of 3 (utilisation 4.9e+03 -> 2.4e+03). State changes along the schedule at P2 0.135->0.068 mm: LATENT_UNDER_TENSION / MANIFEST_AFTER_TENSION_RELEASE. Onset stripe height, model stripe: in the mill 1.19 um -> 6.51 um, after release 0.046 um (reporting-threshold limited) -> 0.23 um (reporting-threshold limited). Onset stripe height, Gaussian reference: in the mill 1.11 um -> 6 um, after release 0.0415 um (reporting-threshold limited) -> 0.208 um (reporting-threshold limited). For the model stripe the onsets RISE toward the thin pass (thick/thin ratio 0.18 in the mill, 0.2 after release): in this model the stripe is LESS likely to show at thinner gauge, so the model does not reproduce "worse at thinner gauge" for it. For the Gaussian reference the onsets RISE toward the thin pass (thick/thin ratio 0.18 in the mill, 0.2 after release): in this model the stripe is LESS likely to show at thinner gauge, so the model does not reproduce "worse at thinner gauge" for it. After-release onsets on P1 0.260->0.135 mm, P2 0.135->0.068 mm, P3 0.068->0.035 mm are limited by the 2 I-unit reporting threshold (a band must first be reported), so they are upper bounds of the buckling onset. Flatness dead band half-width 0.271 -> 0.022 I-units. Not assessable (excluded from the trend): P4 0.035->0.018 mm (not derivable (exit gauge 18 um below the 20 um floor of the roll-bite models: chatter.BitePass.validate requires 2e-5 m <= exit thickness)).

thermal_events.attribution_definition: event metrics use the monitor history from the event start to attribution_window_end_s: the start of the next event switching nozzles within the isolation margin (0.1 m) of this one, else the end of the run; a fade beyond it gives only a lower bound (flag FADE_BEYOND_ATTRIBUTION_WINDOW), a later event starting during this one truncates its peak (flag PEAK_TRUNCATED_BY_LATER_EVENT); an earlier event in the same neighbourhood leaves its residual in the history (flag EARLIER_EVENT_IN_SAME_REGION)
thermal_events.band_life_definition: band_life_s = event duration + time after the event ends for the stripe to fall below the manifest threshold (or the reporting threshold when it never becomes manifest)
thermal_events.growth_rate_note: Radius growth follows the radial heat integral, so right after a spray change the stripe grows at 2*alpha*factor*dq/(rho*c) whatever the radial distribution; short-lived bands arise because the stripe crosses the manifest threshold within seconds to tens of seconds and fades over about a minute after the zone returns, not because the roll skin responds fast.
thermal_events.open_discrepancy: The 20 s first-order flatness response identified on a plant (Dohmae & Okamura 2012) is faster than this model's decay; possible causes (none modelled): bite heat depending on the roll surface temperature, emulsion-level heat transfer, per-revolution effects.
thermal_events.stripe_definition: one monitor per connected group of adjacent switched nozzles (a stripe); the stripe with the largest peak radius deviation governs the event metrics (governing_stripe_index), the others are listed under stripes
thermal_events.visible_time_definition: visible_time_s = time above the in-mill manifest threshold if reached, else above the after-release threshold, else above the reporting threshold (visible_time_basis says which); thresholds are stripe heights at the monitor position, from the peak profile scaled (onsets on a >= 10 mm grid)

thermal_steady.stripe_method: difference actual header - healthy header (same pass), thresholded directly (no polynomial de-trend)
